notes:
Intro: PulseFrame builds a VS Code extension aimed at fast in-editor code generation and refactors for mid-sized developer teams. Primary goal is sub-50ms token streaming for inline suggestions and minimal UI jitter.

Use case summary: looking for a streaming-first inference provider that supports model pinning per-release channel (stable/beta/dev), per-user rate limits, and per-organization routing (low-latency region + fallback). Heavy focus on TypeScript/Go code patterns and repository-aware completions. Also wants an embeddings-based local cache for fuzzy search to reduce tokens.

Requirements (customer verbal):
- "We need completions to feel instant — streaming chunks at 20–50ms intervals."
- Must support model version pinning per release channel and predictable latency SLAs for IDE-level UX.
- Granular auth: token scoping for extension vs. server-side agent, SSO via SAML, short-lived keys for mobile/remote dev auth.
- Rate limiting: per-organization and per-developer soft limits; ability to throttle on low-tier seats and burst for paid seats.
- Telemetry: need non-PII usage metrics, per-route latency breakdowns, and opt-out for error telemetry.
- Security: SOC2 equivalent, audit logs, KMS integration, and EU data residency as a stretch goal.

Recent activities (timeline):
- 2026-02-18: Intro call — product fit discussion, demo request for streaming SDK. (owner: Maya)
- 2026-02-24: Technical deep-dive with SE (Liam) — discussed batching, KV cache, and model quantization tradeoffs. Action: Liam to run benchmark on 4k context with 8-bit quantized variant.
- 2026-03-01: Fireflies call ff_20260301_7c2b9e — pulseframe engineering emphasized inline suggestion latency target (<50ms).
- 2026-03-03: Sent security questionnaire; PulseFrame uploaded SAML IdP metadata to drive://redwood/pulseframe/pulseframe-infra-reqs.pdf.
- 2026-03-05: Redwood shared draft POC plan and pricing sketch (drive link). Next: dedicated POC cluster config and signed NDA.

POC scope: 2-week POC on Dedicated (small reserved GPU pool) + streaming SDK integrated into VS Code extension prototype. Measure: median per-chunk latency, tokens/sec sustained at 100 concurrent dev sessions, cost per 1M tokens, fallback behavior under quota exhaustion.

Notes from SE: prefer per-channel model pinning (tagged versions) over free-for-all model rotation; will test Redwood's automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variant when latency spikes. PulseFrame wants simple SDK hooks to manage incremental edits, cancelation, and local prefix cache to avoid repeating expensive prompts.

Quotes / CRM shorthand: "Need it to feel like typing, not waiting." — Lead eng.
"If we can't hit 50ms, user retention drops fast" — PM.

Open items / blockers: waiting on SAML metadata exchange (IdP), legal signoff on DPA, final benchmarking numbers for 8-bit model variants, clarity around per-seat burst pricing.

Next steps (short): schedule dedicated POC kickoff (owner: Maya), exchange NDA, SE to deliver benchmark by 2026-03-12, Redwood to propose rate-limit config templates for extension deployment.
